Rheometry
 AR-G2 TA instrument
The AR-G2 devices are controlled stress rheometers with a magnetic-levitation thrust bearing and a drag cup motor to allow nanotorque control. The devices are suited for testing of melts, fluids and interfaces. A convection oven and peltier-controlled bottom plates and couettes are available for accurate temperature control.
 Read more
 AR2000ex TA Instruments
The AR2000, equipped with electrically heated plates is suited to test viscous fluids, melts, reactive materials and solids in an inert atmosphere. The instrument is currently placed in the quadrivium.
 Read more
 Capillary Breakup Extensional Rheometer
With the CaBER instrument, stringiness, filament breakup-times and extensional viscosities can be quantified to quickly optimize fluid formulations for either industrial or research applications. 
 Read more
 Counterrotating prototype
The counterrotating cell combines a MCR and DSR device to create a stagnation plane during flow to facilitate optical observations. The microscope can be positioned to observe in the velocity gradient as well as in the vorticity direction using parallel plates or a couette cell.
 Read more
 DHR-AR-G2 Double Wall Ring
The AR-G2 and DHR rheometers can be combined with a Du Noüy ring or a Double Wall Ring (DWR) geometry to measure the steady-state and transient interfacial properties of liquid-liquid or liquid-air interfaces. The DWR can be used with a Langmuir trough for compression or expansion.
 Read more
 Discovery HR
The Discovery HR (DHR-2 and DHR-3) is a new, advanced single head controlled stress rheometer, that combines a patented magnetic bearing, drag cup motor, and force rebalance transducer (FRT), to allow excellent torque and normal force control. The devices can be equipped with interfacial setups (see further) and powder set-ups.
 Read more
 Dynamic angle of repose
The variation in angle of the powder surface in a partially filled rotating drum is noted as the resulting AoR index. This technique to measure powder flowability is rather fast, easy to operate, and requires relatively small sample volume. This way, a simple comparison between different powders can be made.
 Read more
 Filament stretching device
Our home-built filament stretching device is capable of delivering constant strain rates that are sufficiently high to measure intermediate viscous systems that have capillary thinning and breaking time scales that are not accessible with current filament stretching devices.
 Read more
 Fixtures for rotational devices
The Extensional Viscosity Fixture (EVF) for the ARES devices is a fiber wind-up technique to measure the uniaxial extensional properties of high viscous polymers. Hencky strains up to 4 and strain rates up to 10 s.
 Read more
 Force rebalance Microgap Rheometer
The Force rebalance Microgap Rheometer (FMR) is an in-house constructed sliding plate device to measure accurately both torques and normal force in narrow gaps. Rheological measurements and optical techniques can be performed simultaneously.
 Read more
 Hausner ratio
With the tapped density tester series JV of Copley, the bulk and tapped powder density or the apparent volume can be determined. From this, the Hausner Ratio or the Compressibility Index of a powder can be obtained and used as an index to compare different powders. 
 Read more
 In-house developed Powder Rheometer
The in-house developed powder rheometry setup is compatible with the TA Instruments stress-controlled devices and consists of a propellor (different types available) performing simultaneously a rotational and axial movement through a powder bed contained in a Peltier-controled cup, allowing temperatures from -20 °C up to 150 °C.
 Read more
 Linkam Optical Shearing System CSS450
The Linkam Optical Shearing System (CSS450) allows structural dynamics of complex fluids to be directly observed via standard optical microscopy or other light techniques under precisely controlled temperature and various shear modes.
 Read more
 Melt Flow Indexer and Rheometer
The rheometer can also be used to determine the material parameters used in simulation software between 60°C to 400°C.
 Read more
 Microscopy & Conoscopy
Several microscopes (bright field, fluorescence, etc.) can be mounted on some of the rotational rheometers. Several flow geometries (Linkam shear cell, eccentric device, counterrotating device, four roll mill, microfluidics, etc.) are available to monitor the structure development in complex flows.
 Read more
 Modular Compact Rheometer MCR300
The Modular Compact Rheometer MCR300 stress controlled rheometer is adapted to combine rheological and optical measurements (turbidity, SALS, birefringence, dichroism) on structured materials.
 Read more
 Modular Compact Rheometer MCR302 WSP
The MCR Without Support Plate (WSP) is a special version of the MCR302 with the front panel shifted to the right side of the instrument allowing a maximum working area below the motor drive. The device is coupled to a VTi confocal microscope (see further) for rheo-confocal measurements.
 Read more
 Modular Compact Rheometer MCR702 twin drive
The MCR702 twin drive rheometers with optical setups are used to combine rheological properties of fluids and optical observations in the stagnation plane during flow. Both glass parallel plates and a glass couette cel are available. Besides optical microscopy setups, also a UV-curing setup is available.
 Read more
 Physica Modular Compact Rheometer 501
Two Physica MCR501 devices are equipped with a fluids bath, Peltier, and oven to measure solutions, biological materials, polymers, etc. Multiple accessories for controlled environments are available.
 Read more
 Rheo-optics
A high resolution polarization modulation setup enables to follow fast changes in the microstructure. Both the linear conservative dichroism and the flow birefringence can be measured.
 Read more
